issues.title: Mobile user blocked after signup by unlabeled create-project button and missing project…

quote.text: That empty button might be a menu toggle

issues.why: After submitting the signup form on mobile, Kwame encountered an unlabeled plus button (element 5) that screen readers announce only as 'button' and a project key field with no label or helper text. He clicked the button three times, filled the fields twice, and waited twice, but nothing changed on screen, so he quit.

fix.summary: Give the create-project button an accessible name and add a label with format guidance to the project key field so mobile users can complete the flow.
fix.before: Unlabeled plus button (element 5) opens project creation; project key textbox (element 9) has no visible label or helper text.
fix.after: Plus button has aria-label='Create new project'; project key field shows label 'Project key' and placeholder 'e.g. PROJ' with auto-generated suggestion.

issues.title: Three identical 'Start free trial' links with no visual distinction between plan tiers
issues.screen_label: Pick the plan that fits your team

quote.text: This looks like the sign up button I need to click to get started.

issues.why: The Starter, Team, and Business cards each contain a 'Start free trial' link (element 10) that looks the same. Users cannot tell which plan they are selecting without reading surrounding context, increasing the risk of choosing the wrong tier.

fix.summary: Differentiate the trial buttons by plan name so users know which tier they are starting.
fix.before: All three plan cards use the identical link text 'Start free trial'.
fix.after: Starter card: 'Start free trial - Starter'; Team card: 'Start free trial - Team'; Business card: 'Start free trial - Business'.

issues.title: Project key field lacks label and format guidance, causing uncertainty

quote.text: I'll enter a project key so I can create the project.

issues.why: The project key textbox (element 9) has no visible label or helper text explaining what a project key is or its expected format. Every user who reached project creation had to guess the value, and Kwame's repeated failures suggest invalid entries blocked submission on mobile.

fix.summary: Add a clear label and placeholder with an auto-generated suggestion to the project key field.
fix.before: Project key input (element 9) has no label or placeholder.
fix.after: Label: 'Project key'; placeholder: 'e.g. PROJ'; pre-fill with an auto-generated uppercase code the user can edit.

issues.title: Payment details required before account creation despite 14-day free trial claim

quote.text: Now filling payment details with test card.

issues.why: The signup form demands credit card information before the account is created, even though the page states a 14-day free trial with no charge until the trial ends. Margaret and Sunita both entered test card numbers to proceed, adding friction and distrust.

fix.summary: Remove the payment step from initial signup; collect payment only when the trial ends or the user chooses to upgrade.
fix.before: Signup form includes required Card number, Expiry, CVC fields and a Submit button that sends payment data.
fix.after: Signup form collects only name, email, password, workspace slug, and terms agreement; payment details are requested later in the trial banner or upgrade flow.

issues.alt: I see a sign up page for Fernhill. I am looking for a way to create my first project. I notice a request for a valid card number and I am confused because I only wanted to sign up and not pay yet.

issues.title: Cookie consent banner covers content and lacks clear dismiss action
issues.screen_label: Projects that stay on track, without the busywork

quote.text: Accept cookies to clear the banner and proceed.

issues.why: The banner at the bottom left obscures page content and the only visible action is 'Accept all' (element 22). Users must interact with it before they can reach the signup flow, adding a mandatory step that feels like a barrier.

fix.summary: Move the banner to a non-obscuring position and add a visible 'Close' or 'Reject' option alongside 'Accept all'.
fix.before: Banner fixed at bottom left covering content; only 'Accept all' button (element 22) is prominent.
fix.after: Banner positioned at top or bottom edge without covering main content; shows 'Accept all', 'Reject all', and 'Manage preferences' with equal visual weight.

expert.screen_label: Projects that stay on track, without the busywork
expert.finding: The cookie consent banner at the bottom left covers the page content and lacks a clear dismiss or close action, leaving users uncertain how to proceed with signup.
expert.suggestion: Add a visible close button or ensure the banner does not obstruct primary calls to action.

expert.finding: The payment details section requires credit card information before account creation, even though the page states there is a 14-day free trial and users won't be charged until the trial ends.
expert.suggestion: Make payment details optional during signup and only collect them before the trial period ends.

expert.screen_label: Projects that stay on track, without the busywork
expert.finding: Multiple navigation links and buttons use identical labels such as 'Get started' and 'Fernhill' without distinguishing context, making it hard to predict where each will lead.
expert.suggestion: Differentiate duplicate labels with context-specific text, for example 'Start free trial' versus 'Return to homepage'.

expert.screen_label: Pick the plan that fits your team
expert.finding: The Monthly/Yearly toggle shows 'Monthly' as selected, but the plan cards display monthly prices and 'Billed monthly' without indicating what the Yearly prices would be, so users cannot see the 20% savings in concrete terms.
expert.suggestion: When Yearly is toggled, update the card prices to show the discounted yearly rate (or monthly equivalent) and the total savings.

expert.screen_label: Pick the plan that fits your team
expert.finding: There are three identical 'Start free trial' links (Starter, Team, Business) with no visual distinction other than surrounding card context, increasing the risk users click the wrong plan tier.
expert.suggestion: Differentiate each CTA by including the plan name or price in the button text, e.g. 'Start Team free trial ($14/user/month)'.

expert.finding: The Submit button is not visible in the screenshot, so users cannot see how to complete the form after filling it out.
expert.suggestion: Ensure the Submit button is visible without scrolling, or indicate that more content exists below.

expert.finding: The 'Getting started' panel marks 'Create your account' as complete with a checkmark, but the user is still on the signup page and has not finished creating an account, which misrepresents progress.
expert.suggestion: Remove the checkmark from 'Create your account' until the signup flow is actually completed.

expert.finding: The central card instructs users to 'Click + next to Projects in the sidebar', but the sidebar section is labeled 'PROJECTS' and the plus button is not visibly adjacent to that label, making the instruction hard to follow.
expert.suggestion: Change the instruction to 'Click the + button under PROJECTS in the sidebar' or visually highlight the sidebar plus button.

expert.finding: The Project key textbox has no visible label or helper text explaining what a project key is or its format, leaving users uncertain what to enter.
expert.suggestion: Add a concise helper text or tooltip under the Project key field explaining its purpose and allowed characters.

expert.finding: The 'Getting started' panel marks 'Create your account' as complete with a checkmark, but the user is still on the signup page and the account creation task is not actually finished, creating false confidence.
expert.suggestion: Remove the checkmark from 'Create your account' until the signup flow is completed, or change the label to reflect the current step.

expert.finding: The central empty state instructs users to 'Click + next to Projects in the sidebar', but the sidebar 'PROJECTS' section header has no visible plus icon; the only visible plus is a floating button lower in the sidebar, so users cannot…
expert.suggestion: Add a visible plus button directly beside the 'PROJECTS' heading in the sidebar, or change the instruction to point to the actual floating plus button.

expert.finding: The 'Create' button is enabled while the 'Project name' field is empty, giving no indication that the field is required before submission.
expert.suggestion: Disable the 'Create' button until the 'Project name' field contains valid input, or show inline validation when the user attempts to submit.

expert.finding: The 'Project key' textbox is empty with no format guidance or auto-generation, so users may enter an invalid key and receive an error after clicking 'Create'.
expert.suggestion: Add placeholder text or helper text describing the required key format (e.g., uppercase letters only), or auto-generate a key from the project name.

expert.finding: A form field has no label (“Work email”). Placeholder text disappears as soon as you type.
expert.suggestion: Add a visible <label> tied to the field with for/id; keep the placeholder only as an example.

expert.finding: Tap target (“Fernhill”; “Log in”; “Change” +1 more) is smaller than 40×40 px on a phone. Measured: 107×31px.
expert.suggestion: Make interactive elements at least 44×44 px (min-height/min-width or padding).

expert.finding: Low-contrast text (“+ Add task”; “AK”; “Blank template” +22 more). Measured: 2.7:1 (needs 4.5:1).
expert.suggestion: Darken the text or lighten the background to reach at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

expert.suggestion: Give icon-only buttons an aria-label (e.g. aria-label="Close") or visible text.

expert.screen_label: Projects that stay on track, without the busywork
expert.finding: The 'Manage preferences' button in the cookie banner has no visible confirmation or feedback after being clicked, so users cannot tell if their choice was saved.
expert.suggestion: Provide a brief confirmation message or visual state change when preferences are saved.

expert.screen_label: Projects that stay on track, without the busywork
expert.finding: The top navigation and footer navigation contain overlapping but inconsistently ordered links, such as 'Product' versus 'Features' and 'How it works' versus '#how'.
expert.suggestion: Align terminology and order across header and footer navigation to match user expectations.

expert.screen_label: Pick the plan that fits your team
expert.finding: The accordion questions (e.g. 'What happens when my trial ends?') are visible but their answers are hidden, forcing users to click and remember information across interactions.
expert.suggestion: Show short answer summaries directly under each question, or expand the most relevant FAQ (trial ending) by default.

expert.screen_label: Pick the plan that fits your team
expert.finding: The footer contains links to Guides, About, Status, Careers, and Contact that point to '#' placeholders instead of real pages, which is inconsistent with the working header navigation.
expert.suggestion: Replace the '#' hrefs with actual URLs or remove the placeholder links until the pages exist.

expert.finding: The Workspace slug field shows 'fernhill.app/' as a prefix inside the input, which may confuse users about what portion they need to type.
expert.suggestion: Display 'fernhill.app/' as static text outside the input field so users only enter the custom slug portion.

expert.finding: The success banner states three starter tasks were added, but the board columns show only two tasks in To do and one in Doing, creating a mismatch that confuses the user about actual project state.
expert.suggestion: Update the banner text to match the actual task count or ensure all three tasks are visible on the board.

expert.finding: The Inbox navigation link displays a badge with the number 2, but no other navigation items use badges, making the pattern inconsistent and its meaning unclear.
expert.suggestion: Either apply badges consistently to other navigation items with pending counts or remove the badge from Inbox.

expert.finding: The sidebar shows the workspace name as Fernworkspace while the page title and URL reference Fernhill, creating brand inconsistency that forces users to remember which name is correct.
expert.suggestion: Align the workspace branding across the sidebar, page title, and URL to use a single consistent name.

expert.finding: The Upgrade link in the bottom trial banner is visually emphasized while the primary call-to-action buttons on the board are secondary in style, which may lead users to click upgrade prematurely instead of adding tasks.
expert.suggestion: Make the Add task buttons more visually prominent than the Upgrade link to guide users toward the core task creation flow.

expert.finding: The 'Upgrade' link in the bottom trial banner is underlined like a primary action, but the user's goal is to create a project, so this prominent link may cause accidental navigation away from the task.
expert.suggestion: Restyle the 'Upgrade' link as a secondary text link or move it away from the main onboarding area.

expert.finding: The Create button is enabled even though the Project name and Project key fields are empty, allowing users to submit an incomplete form and likely receive an error.
expert.suggestion: Disable the Create button until both required fields contain valid input, then enable it once the form is complete.

expert.finding: The sidebar badge on Inbox shows the number 2, but the link text itself reads Inbox 2, duplicating the count and creating redundant, confusing labeling.
expert.suggestion: Remove the duplicate number from the link label so it simply reads Inbox, keeping the badge as the sole count indicator.

expert.finding: The Project name field only shows placeholder text with no persistent label, so the context disappears once the user starts typing.
expert.suggestion: Add a visible Project name label above the input field in addition to the placeholder hint.

expert.finding: The 'Upgrade' link in the top navigation and the 'Upgrade' link in the bottom trial banner both lead to pricing.html, but there is no confirmation or warning before navigating away from the signup setup, risking accidental abandonment of…
expert.suggestion: Add a confirmation dialog or inline warning when clicking 'Upgrade' during onboarding to prevent accidental navigation away from project creation.

expert.finding: The 'Inbox' sidebar item shows a badge with the number 2, but the navigation link is labeled 'Inbox 2', duplicating the count in the label and the badge, which is inconsistent with the other nav items that have no such duplication.
expert.suggestion: Remove the number from the 'Inbox 2' link label and keep only the badge, or remove the badge and keep the label, to match the pattern of other navigation items.

expert.finding: The template cards use icons and short labels without clear visual distinction between the selected 'Blank' state and unselected states beyond a subtle border, making the selection less obvious.
expert.suggestion: Apply a stronger selected state (e.g., filled background or checkmark) to the active template card to make the choice immediately recognizable.

expert.finding: The sidebar shows 'Inbox' with a notification badge of 2, but the top navigation link is labeled 'Inbox 2', creating inconsistent naming for the same destination.
expert.suggestion: Rename the top navigation link to 'Inbox' to match the sidebar label and remove the redundant number.
